questions.q_en: Ratio of present age of P to Q is 3 : 4. After 3 years the ratio becomes 7 : 9. What will be the age of Q after 5 years?
questions.solution_en:
Let the ages of P and Q be 3x years and 4x years respectively.

According to question,

(3x + 3)/(4x + 3) = 7/9

=> 27x + 27 = 28x + 21

=> x = 6

Age of Q after 5 years = 4 * 6 + 5 = 29 years

questions.q_en: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank at 6 liters/minute, 3 liters/minute and 4 liters/minute respectively. When all three the pipes are opened together, they can fill 52% of the tank in 9.6 minutes. What is the capacity of the tank (in liters)?
questions.solution_en:
Let the capacity of the tank = x liters

Then, time taken by pipe A alone to fill the tank = x/6 minutes

Time taken by pipe B alone to fill the tank = x/3 minutes

Time taken by pipe C alone to fill the tank = x/4 minutes

Part of the tank filled by all three pipes together in one minute

= (6/x + 3/x + 4/x)

= 13/x

When all three the pipes are opened together, they can fill 52% of the tank in 9.6 minutes. Then,

9.6 = (52/100) * (x/13)

x = 240

questions.q_en: A worker increases his efficiency by 20% and completes a task of 120 units in 6 days. How many days would he have taken to complete the task at his original efficiency?
questions.solution_en:
Let the original efficiency be 'r'

Increased efficiency = 1.2r.

Increased Rate = Work / Time => 1.2r = 120 / 6 = 20 units/day.

Original efficiency r = 20 / 1.2 = 50/3 units/day.

Time at original efficiency = 120 / (50/3) = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.q_en: Cost of drink A per litre is 3/5 of the cost of drink B per litre. A man wanted to buy certain quantity of drink A and 8 litres of drink B. But by mistake, the quantity of drink A and drink B got exchanged so the man is ended up paying 40% more. How much quantity of drink A did he wants to buy?
questions.solution_en:
Cost of drink B per litre = ₹5a

Cost of drink A per litre = ₹3a

Let the quantity of drink A bought by man = 'b' litres

Original cost = b*3a + 8*5a = a(3b + 40)

Cost after exchange = 8*3a + b*5a = a(24 + 5b)

Now,

a(24 + 5b) = 140% of a(3b + 40)

5(24 + 5b) = 7(3b + 40)

4b = 160

b = 40

So, the quantity of drink A he wants to buy = 40 litres

questions.q_en: A vertical pole and a vertical tower stand on the same level of ground. From the top of the pole, the angle of elevation to the top of the tower is 60°, and the angle of depression to the bottom of the tower is 30°. Given that the height of the tower is 276 meters, determine the height of the pole.
questions.solution_en:
Let the height of the pole be 'H' m.

Let the distance between the pole and the tower = 'D' m

tan30° = H/D

1/√3 = H/D

H√3 = D

tan 60° = (276 - H) /D

√3 = (276 - H) /D

√3 = (276 - H)/H√3

√3 X H√3 = 276 - H

3H + H = 276

H = 69 m

questions.q_en: How much water should be added to 60 litres of milk at 1(1/2) litres a rupee so as to have a mixture worth 1(7/8) litres a rupee?
questions.solution_en:
Cost of 1 litre of milk:

1(1/2)litres for 1 rupee → cost per litre = 1 ÷ 1.5 = 2/3 rupee.

Total cost of 60 litres of milk = 60 X (2/3) = 40 rupees.

Desired cost per litre of the mixture:

1(7/8) litres for 1 rupee → 1.875 litres per rupee → cost per litre = 1 ÷ 1.875 = 8/15 rupee.

Let x = litres of water (free).

Total volume = 60 + x.

Total cost remains 40 rupees (milk only).

New cost per litre = 40 ÷ (60 + x).

Set this equal to 8/15: 40 ÷ (60 + x) = 8/15.

Cross multiply: 40 X 15 = 8 X (60 + x) → 600 = 480 + 8x → x = 15.

Option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en: Shikha sold a handbag at the price 11% above the cost price. If she had bought it at 8% less than what she actually paid for it and sold it at the price which is Rs. y more than the actual selling price, then she would have gained 25%. Find the ratio of value of y to the original cost price of the handbag.
questions.solution_en:
Let cost price of handbag = Rs. 100

In first condition,

Selling price of handbag = 100* (100 + 11)/100 = Rs.111

In second condition,

New cost price of handbag = 100* (100 - 8)/100 = Rs.92

New selling price of handbag = 92* (100 + 25)/100 = 92* 5/4 = Rs.115

ATQ,

y = 115 - 111

y = 4

Required ratio = 4: 100 = 1: 25

questions.q_en: A is 36 years old and his brother is 9 years older than A. What was the ratio of the ages of A and his brother fifteen years ago?

A is 36 years old

Age of A's brother = 36 + 9 = 45 years.

The ratio of the ages of A and his brother fifteen years ago = (36 - 15) / (45 - 15) = 21/30 = 7/10.

questions.q_en:
The pie chart given below shows the degree distribution of number of students attempted six mock tests from a learning platform:

Number of students who attempted mock test T5 = 11700

M = Average number of students who attempted tests T2, T4, and T6.

N = Difference between the number of students who attempted test T1, and T3.

What is the value of M ÷ N?
questions.solution_en:
Number of students who attempted all six mock tests = 11700 * 360/39 = 108000

Average number of students who attempted tests T2, T4, and T6 = 108000/3 * (72 + 96 + 30)/360 = 19800

Difference between the number of students who attempted test T1, and T3 = 108000 * (78 - 45)/360 = 9900

So, M/N = 19800/9900 = 2

Alternate method

Average number of students who attempted tests T2, T4 and T6 = (72 + 96 +30)/3 = 66

Difference between the number of students who attempted test T1 and T3 = 78 - 45 = 33

So, M/N = 66/33 = 2

"

Pipe A is» emptying at 3 units/hr

When filling pipe 'B' start function. then emptying rate comes down to 2 unit/hr So filling pipe efficiency is = 3-2 = 1 units/hr
